data.title: Meduza: See the damage to the Crimean Bridge after Ukraine’s strikes: New video filmed from a passing train reveals a massive gap in the roadway
data.summary: On the morning of November 18, a video began circulating on social media showing footage of a destroyed span of the Crimean Bridge after strikes by the Ukrainian military. The Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova+ published the footage, filmed from a train traveling along the railway section of the bridge, which runs parallel to the roadway. The train takes almost 30 seconds to pass the gap left where the span once stood. Ukraine struck the bridge on two consecutive nights, November 16 and 17. After the first attack, the Kremlin said the damage was “minor”; after the second, Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt and would be “even better than before.” Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack on the Crimean Bridge an “unprecedented operation” that had been in preparation for several weeks. The last strike on the bridge, according to Zelensky, was carried out with Neptune, Flamingo, and Ruta missiles.
